name: m5-uniques-uncache

variantDescriptions.weak: `claude/uniques-audit` `dfba9ad593` (retronym/scala#212 + #239 + census probe, census off) with today's `WeakHashSet` table
variantDescriptions.uncache-four: chunked-weak, and new types made inside boolean type queries (`isSubType`, `isSameType`, `matchesType`, `specializesSym`), `adapt`'s polymorphic instantiation, `narrowForFindMember` and `stableTypeFor` are not interned: shared only if already in the table or in a 4096-slot direct-mapped cache
variantDescriptions.uncache-all: as uncache-four, plus type maps that clone params, existential packing, `Mixin.cloneBeforeErasure` and `instantiateTypeParams`

description: Does not interning the types made in weak scopes pay? From the census of [retronym/scala#239](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/239) on retronym/scala#212's completion frames: 80–99% of the types those scopes intern are collected within the run. Locally (scalap, re2s), output is byte-identical, and the table's inserts fall by 16–27% (four scopes) and 47–64% (all). The risk is lost sharing of per-instance caches (`baseTypeSeqCache`, ...) on rebuilt types; the direct-mapped cache catches most repeats (lost sharing: 200 of 8.5K new instances on scalap with four scopes, 2.5K of 31K with all).
Same setup as `m4-chunked-uniques` (job 539). The weak scopes are only tracked in the uncache variants, so their bookkeeping counts against them.

Laptop copy of `m4-uniques-uncache` while the M4 is held by a paused job: read instructions/op and `cyc%:gc` before time (endpoint security moves cycles at equal instructions here). 3 rounds, load gate at 3 cores.
